concepts.title: Blood: Plasma and Formed Elements
concepts.definition: Blood is a connective tissue of plasma with water, proteins and minerals, and formed elements of erythrocytes carrying haemoglobin, leucocytes of granulocytes and agranulocytes for immunity, and cell fragments called blood platelets for coagulation.
concepts.key_idea: Plasma proteins like fibrinogen, globulins and albumins serve clotting, immunity and osmotic balance, while erythrocytes lack a nucleus in mammals and carry about 12-16 g of haemoglobin per 100 ml in a healthy adult.

concepts.title: Blood Groups, Rh Factor and Coagulation
concepts.definition: ABO blood grouping depends on antigens on RBCs and antibodies in plasma, the Rh factor distinguishes Rh positive from Rh negative persons and matters in erythroblastosis fetalis, and coagulation converts fibrinogen to fibrin through thrombin with platelets and calcium ions at the injury site.
concepts.key_idea: Universal donor blood of group O and universal recipient blood of group AB follow from the antigen-antibody matching, and heparin acts as an anticoagulant in the body.

solution_steps.explain: Note antigens on the RBC surface and antibodies in the plasma.

concepts.title: Human Heart, Cardiac Cycle and Cardiac Output
concepts.definition: The human heart is a four chambered myogenic pump with nodal tissue of SA node and AV node; the cardiac cycle of joint diastole, atrial systole and ventricular systole lasts about 0.8 seconds, and cardiac output equals stroke volume of about 70 ml multiplied by heart rate of about 72 beats per minute, giving nearly 5 litres per minute.
concepts.key_idea: The sounds lub and dub mark closure of the tricuspid and bicuspid valves and the semilunar valves respectively, and the heart beats about 100000 times a day.

solution_steps.action: multiply stroke volume by heart rate
solution_steps.explain: Multiply the stroke volume by the number of heart beats per minute to get the cardiac output

concepts.title: ECG, Double Circulation and Disorders
concepts.definition: An electrocardiogram records the P wave of atrial depolarisation, the QRS complex of ventricular depolarisation and the T wave of ventricular repolarisation; humans show double circulation with pulmonary and systemic circuits separately, and circulatory disorders include hypertension, coronary artery disease, angina and heart failure.
concepts.key_idea: Blood pressure of a healthy person is measured as systolic over diastolic pressure of 120 over 80 mm Hg, and persistent 140 over 90 or higher counts as hypertension.

solution_steps.explain: Match P, QRS and T deflections to atrial and ventricular events.
